$comment: Anti-patterns for enhanced prompts. Used by scripts/validate.mjs (rules with selfCheck: true are applied to prompt-engine's own instruction files), by scripts/build.mjs, which turns them into the eval graders evals/*/graders/lint-prompt*.md, and by the MCP server's check_prompt tool, which matches each pattern one line at a time, after turning each control character into a space and each run of whitespace into one space (so a rule about tabs or double spaces never fires there). Patterns are JavaScript regular expressions; 'flags' are passed to new RegExp(). check_prompt skips a rule whose pattern repeats without a bound, more than {0,200} times or a group (a ? after a group is fine), uses a backreference, can match the empty string, has more than 1,000 ways to match from one position, looks at more than 300 characters, or takes more than 1,000 steps to try every way to match from one position; CONTRIBUTING.md explains each limit. scripts/test/lint-rules.test.mjs separately times every rule on adversarial input.

rules.message: Capitalized pressure words can make current models over-apply the rule. Write it plainly and give the reason; keep 'always' and 'never' for true invariants.

Asks the model to think step by step or to show its reasoning. Prompt Engine leaves such requests out for every target, as a rule of its own. Ask for the result plus a brief explanation or evidence instead.
Magic phrases and generic personas add little. Use effort or reasoning settings where available, and a specific role only when it changes the answer.
Prefilled assistant turns are an API setting, and current Claude models don't support them. Describe the output format instead.
An unfilled template variable. Replace it, or use a [[placeholder]] the user knows to fill.
Placeholder still open. List it under 'Fill before running' and fill it before the prompt is used.
Generic quality tags carry little meaning for natural-language image and video models. Name concrete materials, light sources and framing instead.
